jobs.description:
Department of Geosciences and Natural Resource Management and Department of Biology, invites applicants for three two-year Postdoc positions within forest microbiome manipulation. The positions are part of the project “MycoForest - Stimulating Forest carbon uptake and storage by mycorrhizal inoculation”, which is financed under the Innomission partnership INNO-CCUS by Innovation Fund Denmark.
 
 Start date is 1 February 2027, or as soon as possible thereafter.
 
 The project
 The soil microbiome plays a crucial role in soil- and ecosystem functioning including ecosystem carbon sequestration and support of plant nutrient acquisition.
 
 Denmark is devoted to become carbon neutral by 2045/2050, a goal involving a significant role for biological carbon sequestration and storage. A part of the Danish strategy to reach carbon neutrality is to afforest former agricultural land thereby increasing biological ecosystem carbon capture and storage. However, agricultural soils do not harbor an optimal microbiome for initial tree growth and forest ecosystem development. This may lead to increased mortality, reduced tree growth and slower development of forest soil functions and ultimately non-optimal carbon capture, especially in the early stages of afforestation.
 
 Therefore, the MycoForest project aims to manipulate and assist the microbiome of agricultural soils through mycorrhizal inoculation as an integrated part of tree planting to stimulate tree growth and carbon sequestration. Therefore, MycoForest at University of Copenhagen is hiring three postdocs to become part of this novel journey towards increased biological carbon sequestration and to play key roles in the scientific investigations.
 
 Each of the three postdocs will cover one of three distinct areas of fundamental importance to understand and document the role of the microbiome in afforestation.
 
 The three key areas are:

   	
• Microbial and mycorrhizal fungal development 	
• Soil functioning and soil carbon dynamics 	
• Tree survival and growth, and carbon uptake   
 The studies will involve controlled greenhouse as well as field scale experiments, and the three postdocs will each be responsible for one of the three specific parts of the project. At the same time, they will be closely linked to each other through tight collaboration on establishment and sampling of the afforestation experiment. The postdoc positions will start as soon as possible and will run for 2 years. For the requirements of the specific postdocs, please see the descriptions below.
 
 Contact: Specific questions for each of the postdocs, please see below. For general MycoForest questions, please contact Claus Beier, cbe@ign.ku.dk.
 
 Postdoc 1 – Soil microbial development after mycorrhizal inoculation
 The post doc will oversee the formulation and addition of fungal or other types of inoculums and will follow and quantify the mycorrhizal fungal colonization of seedlings, root and soil. Experimentation will be both in mesocosm/greenhouse conditions and in the field. Colonization will be followed in different soils and host trees with a combination of classical microscopic techniques and novel molecular methods. The studies aim to document successful establishment of mycorrhizal fungi within the indigenous communities.
 
 Therefore, we are looking for candidates with specific knowledge and hands-on with:

   	
• Fungi in general including mycorrhizal fungi, preferentially ectomycorrhiza 	
• Field experience in general, handling and sorting soils and roots in specific 	
• Microscopy, especially stereo microscopy of roots 	
• DNA extraction og plants and soil and PCR optimizations including qPCR 	
• Bioinformatics and statistical analysis of meta-barcoding datasets   
 The post doc will work closely together with PD 2 and 3 for plant and soil responses to inoculations.
 
 Principal supervisor is Associate Professor Rasmus Kjøller, Department of Biology, rasmusk@bio.ku.dk, Phone: +45 35322311
 
 Postdoc 2 – Soil functioning and soil carbon dynamics in response to mycorrhizal inoculation
 The post doc will study effects of inoculation in different soil types and tree species on soil carbon processes including formation of persistent SOC fractions.  The postdoc will study soil carbon dynamics in mesocosm/greenhouse conditions in close cooperation with postdoc 1 and in field experimental conditions in cooperation with postdoc 3. The project will address how inoculation and changes in the mycorrhizal community composition will affect soil carbon sequestration processes in post-agricultural soils. The studies will shed light on the extent to which inoculation with forest-associated mycorrhiza and forest soil will change the soil C input quantity and quality from roots and microbial necromass, eventually enhancing accumulation of persistent forms of SOC. 
 
 We are looking for a candidate with a PhD in the fields of soil science and organic matter studies, soil ecology and biogeochemistry. Previous experience with plant-soil interactions in field, mesocosm and laboratory experiments using chemical soil analyses including soil organic carbon (organic matter fractionation and biomarkers targeting microbial and plant origin of organic matter), carbon isotopes, roots, and microbial taxonomic and functional community composition will be considered a plus.
 
 Principal supervisor is Professor Lars Vesterdal, Department of Geosciences and Natural Resource Management, lv@ign.ku.dk, Phone: +45 61670865
 
 Postdoc 3 – Tree responses to mycorrhiza inoculation
 The postdoc will establish and follow field experiments in practical afforestation sites and monitor plant responses such as growth and survival, mycorrhizal colonization, and plant community development.
 
 The studies will address the potential of inoculation with forest-associated mycorrhiza and forest soil to stimulate survival, growth and carbon draw down of forest trees and communities including the role of tree species and soil type interactions. 
 
 We are looking for highly motivated candidates with a PhD in plant or forestry science and interest and experience in:

   	
• Afforestation, forestry and forest ecology 	
• Design and analysis of experiments 	
• Field work and practical application of technology in land management    
 Principal supervisor is Associate Professor Niclas Scott Bentsen, Department of Geosciences and Natural Resource Management, nb@ign.ku.dk, Phone: +45 20206318.
 
 General qualifications
 Apart from the specific qualifications and interests listed above, we look for candidates with general competences in:

   	
• Driver license (mandatory) 	
• Handling of plants and soil 	
• Organizing and conducting field sampling 	
• Data management 	
• Statistics 	
• Scientific writing and publishing   
 Our groups and research – and what do we offer?
 The positions are located in three different groups at the university.
 
 Postdoc 1 is with Department of Biology, Fungal Ecology lab within Section of Terrestrial Ecology. The group works with/focuses on mycorrhizal fungal communities and their impact on ecosystem processes and plant health. We apply molecular markers to disentangle these otherwise invisible fungal populations and communities associated with plants and soil. Besides molecular markers, we also apply biochemical markers as well as classic microscopy and microbiological culturing of fungi. Another methodological strongpoint is various mesh-enclosure techniques to study and compartmentalize both the function and community composition of mycorrhizal fungal mycelia in soil.
 
 Postdoc 2 and 3 are with Department of Geosciences and Natural Resource Management, one in the Biogeochemistry group and one in the Silviculture, Trees and Bioresources group. In the Biogeochemistry Group we are dedicated to improving the understanding of ecosystem functioning with particular focus on how ecosystems will respond to environmental changes and to management actions. We quantify the pools and fluxes of matter in semi-natural and managed ecosystems and measure the processes related to input and output fluxes in control of soil C stocks to answer questions such as “Can we sequester C in soils by afforestation of cropland soils, and how does this interact with the soil fauna and microbes when using certain tree species or tree species mixtures?” The Silviculture, Trees and Bioresources group encompas expertise in forestry, ecological restoration, growth modelling and systems analysis. The group is dedicated to advance the understanding, development, and management of forest ecosystems to support a wide range of ecosystem services, including carbon storage, material and energy provision, groundwater regulation, and biodiversity conservation.
 
 Department of Biology is located at Norre Campus and Department of Geosciences on Frederiksberg Campus, close to central Copenhagen. The departments offer creative and stimulating working conditions in dynamic and international research environments. The departments are planning to increase their focus on the climate change mitigation potential of forests in upcoming projects. We therefore welcome applications from candidates with a broader interest in the intersection of forests, forest-based climate solutions, biosphere-atmosphere interaction, and related themes.
 
 Responsibilities and tasks

   	
• Carry out independent research projects under the PI’s supervision and in close collaboration with the other PostDocs and researchers within the MycoForest project. 	
• Report and disseminate the periodic progress and results 	
• Take part in relevant teaching activities 	
• Write scientific papers aimed at relevant journals 	
• Actively take part in the research environments at the departments, sections and within the project.   
 We are looking for the following further qualifications:

   	
• Strong ability to interpret data and think analytically, critically, and conceptually. 	
• Strong social competence including interpersonal skills, teamwork and networking ability, and presentation skills 	
• Strong personal competence including autonomy, goal-oriented mind-set, planning/organizing/prioritizing, perseverance, problem-solving skills 	
• General personal leadership skills including ability to translate long-term goals to daily work situations (strategic time managing); be flexible to adjust one’s own behavior and thinking according to the (relevant/local) context so as to attain the desired goals (learning ability) 	
• Good language skills and fluency in English   
 Terms of employment
 Employment is full-time and for 2 years.
 
 The position is covered by the Memorandum on Job Structure for Academic Staff.
 
 Terms of appointment and payment accord to the agreement between the Ministry of Finance and The Danish Confederation of Professional Associations on Academics in the State.
 
 Negotiation for salary supplement is possible.
 
 You can read more about salary levels in the state sector www.loenoverblik.dk (in Danish).
 
 Application and Assessment Procedure
 Your application including all attachments must be in English and indicate which of the 3 positions you are applying for.
 
 The application is submitted electronically by clicking APPLY NOW below.
 
 Please include:

   	
• Motivated letter of application (max. one page) – please relate how the above required abilities are represented in your past work experiences 	
• Curriculum vitae including information about your education, experience, language skills and other skills relevant for the position 	
• Original diplomas for Bachelor’s or master’s and PhD and transcript of records in the original language, including an authorized English translation if issued in another language than English or Danish. If not completed, a certified/signed copy of a recent transcript of records or a written statement from the institution or supervisor is accepted. 	
• Publication list 	
• Reference letters (if available)   
 Application deadline:
 The deadline for applications is 2 November 2026, 23:59 GMT +1.
 
 We reserve the right not to consider material received after the deadline, and not to consider applications that do not live up to the abovementioned requirements.
 
 The further process
 After deadline, a number of applicants will be selected for academic assessment by an unbiased expert assessor. You are notified whether you will be passed for assessment.
 
 The assessor will assess the qualifications and experience of the shortlisted applicants with respect to the above mentioned research area, techniques, skills and other requirements. The assessor will conclude whether each applicant is qualified. The assessed applicants will have the opportunity to comment on their assessment. You can read about the recruitment process at https://employment.ku.dk/faculty/recruitment-process/.
 
 Interviews with selected candidates are expected to be held in week 49-50 2026.
 
 Applicants must be prepared for further security screening related to international research collaborations as part of the recruitment process, when UCPH considers it appropriate from a holistic consideration
 
 Questions
 For specific information about the Postdoc position, please contact the principal supervisor.

jobs.occupation: Postdoctoral position in breast cancer epidemiology / clinical epidemiology
jobs.description:
The Department of Clinical Epidemiology at Faculty of Health at Aarhus University invites applications for a position as postdoctoral research fellow in the field of Breast Cancer Epidemiology as per 15 February 2027 or as soon as possible thereafter. This is a two-year position is fully funded by the Health Insurance Denmark.

The Department of Clinical Epidemiology is a research department at Aarhus University Hospital, within the Institute of Clinical Medicine at Aarhus University. Researchers in the department use advanced epidemiological methods to study the prognosis of patient populations. The department is engaged in a variety of activities regarding clinical epidemiological research, including cancer prognosis research. The department is involved in counselling health care professionals to improve the quality of health care and treatment. A large number of projects in the department are carried out in cooperation with Danish and international collaborators.

About the research project
The position entails research within clinical epidemiology, specifically within breast cancer and breast cancer survivorship. The successful candidate will join a project focusing on studies related to adherence to breast cancer treatment; side effects and complications of breast cancer and its treatment; and how these may influence quality of life, long-term survivorship, and early and late breast cancer recurrence. The project investigates the association of pharmacological, genetic and socioeconomic factors and adherence to cancer treatment; employing advanced epidemiological methods including emulated target trials, group-based trajectory modelling, mediation analyses, and Bayesian modelling approaches to investigate adherence to cancer treatment and recurrence. The research fellow will join a vibrant and dynamic multinational and multidisciplinary project team (the Predictors of Breast Cancer Recurrence – ProBeCaRe – project team) with established successful long-term research collaboration. 

The successful applicant will contribute to the development of the department through research of high international quality. They will work closely with colleagues, receiving supervision and guidance. Emphasis will be placed on the applicant’s interest in building bridges between clinical, epidemiological and biostatistical research.

The main tasks will consist of:

• Research in clinical epidemiology, specifically within breast cancer and breast cancer survivorship.
• Make applications as needed for access to Danish population-based and medical registries.
• Independently perform statistical analysis using programmes such as R, SAS, or equivalent.
• Collaborate within an active research group with national and international collaborators.
• Contribute to teaching at the Aarhus University and its collaborators, as necessary.
• Take part in grant writing and participate actively in research fundraising.
• Gain experience supervising students.
• Conduct independent research of high international quality, including publication.
• Write scientific articles and participate in international congresses.
• Perform other tasks within the Department of Clinical Epidemiology fields of interest. Please see our webpage at www.kea.au.dk.
Your competences
You have academic qualifications at PhD/DSc level preferably within one or more of the following areas: epidemiology, clinical epidemiology, cancer epidemiology, public health, biostatistics, and/or can document familiarity with epidemiological research at an international level. Research experience in cancer and pharmacologic research would be advantageous, but not essential. Research experience in epidemiologic methods, analysing and incorporating data from Danish registries, including data from the National Clinical Quality Cancer Databases (specifically data from the Danish Breast Cancer Group), the Health Services Register, and the National Patient Registry, would be useful, particularly data incorporating socioeconomic factors. Research experience in cancer survivorship, patient reported outcomes and national surveys would be a benefit as well. Evidence of the ability to secure competitive research grants would be advantageous. As a person, you are motivated, ambitious, take ownership and possess good communication and interpersonal skills. We expect you to be fluent in oral and written English, with good knowledge of Danish.

In order to be assessed as qualified for this position, you must meet these academic criteria.

Shortlisting will be used.

Expected start date and duration of employment

Job description
We are hiring an Academic Employee for Integrated Carbon Observation System (ICOS) and GEM/Geobasis activities at the Zackenberg Research Station. You will oversee all aspects of operations, including:

• Maintenance and supervision of eddy covariance stations and other monitoring stations in the field.
• Processing and analysis of eddy covariance, meteorological, and vegetation sampling data.
• Communicating and collaborating with the ICOS Ecosystem Thematic Center.
You will also go on extended field trips to harsh, remote locations in Northeast Greenland.

Your profile
You have a master's degree in Physical Geography, Environmental Science, Geophysics, or a similar field.

Experience in fieldwork, maintaining advanced measurement systems, and handling large datasets is required. Practical experience with eddy covariance systems and data loggers, and prior knowledge of ICOS standards and protocols, are an advantage. Experience with GIS software and programming languages such as Python or R is also a strong asset.

We encourage everyone interested to apply, regardless of background. We want to hire the best qualified candidate and will consider a broad range of competencies relevant to every part of the position, with a focus on collaborative skills.

Who we are
The Department of Ecoscience is project-based and does research, talent development, and consultancy across all major biological sub-disciplines. Our research areas include ecosystem ecology (including Arctic environments and ecosystems), aquatic biology and ecology, and biodiversity and conservation biology. The Department currently employs approximately 280 academic and technical staff.

The Department has a strong position in international biodiversity, nature, and environmental research and is a national leader in research-based consultancy in both Denmark and Greenland. Our research examines how ecological framework conditions, historical conditions, natural processes, and human-caused changes in nature and the environment affect surrounding nature. We study the underlying ecological and geographical mechanisms and human impact on biodiversity and ecosystems, with particular attention to how current climate change and other global human-caused environmental changes affect nature and biodiversity.

The Department is a leading adviser to the Danish and Greenlandic authorities on environmental issues. It also leads the Greenland Ecosystem Monitoring (GEM) programme, which focuses on the effects of climate change on Arctic ecosystems. The Zackenberg Research Station is one of GEM's central research sites.

We offer a 2-year position to safeguard our greenhouse gas flux monitoring at Zackenberg in Northeast Greenland National Park. You will join the ICOS and Geobasis teams and the research community at Zackenberg.

The Department of Ecoscience offers an informal research environment and has a long tradition of collaborating with leading international university partners. The working environment is built on teamwork and close working relationships, with established professional and social networks for young scientists. The Department of Nordic Studies and Linguistics, Faculty of Humanities, University of Copenhagen (UCPH), Denmark, invites applications for a two-year postdoctoral fellowship in Computational Lexicography and Linguistics to be filled by the 1st of March 2027 or as soon as possible thereafter.

  The Department of Nordic Studies and Linguistics is home to 1600 students and 160 members of staff. It provides the setting for international research and education from BA to PhD studies within language, language technology, Natural Language Processing, literature, media, culture, and gender studies.

  The successful candidate will be attached to both the Centre for Language Technology (CST), which is one of the research centres of the department, and to the Society of Danish language and Literature (DSL) which compiles and publishes dictionaries and language technology resources for Danish at a scholarly basis, often in research projects in collaboration with CST. The latter affiliation will amount to around six months of the total hiring period of 24 months.

  CST conducts research in different areas of interest for language technology, such as Natural Language Processing, construction of NLP resources, Computational Cognitive Modeling and Multimodality, NLP infrastructure and policy, Representation Learning for NLP and Digital Humanities, among others.  It has a strong international profile, at the same time as pursuing the development of language technology methods and resources for the Danish language. The Centre has considerable experience managing international research projects, frequently attracts visiting researchers, and has organised major conferences in the field. In collaboration with the Department of Computer Science at the University of Copenhagen, it offers an international MSc programme in IT and Cognition. The programme, which currently admits about 30 students a year, comprises a range of courses in Natural Language Processing and Cognitive Science. In addition, we teach at several BA programs and electives, such as the BA ‘Kognitions- and Datavidenskab’ hosted at the Department of Psychology and an elective package on Language-Centric AI for students in the Humanities.

  Job content
 The successful candidate will contribute to the project ELEXAI, which focuses on a European Lexicographic Infrastructure for Artificial Intelligence (https://www.eurac.edu/en/projects/elexai), granted by the European Commission under the Horizon Europe Program.

  The candidate will in particular contribute to the project’s work packages on LLM Benchmarking, the so-called LexBench, which is led by CST and also involves DSL. This part of the project investigates how benchmarks for Natural Language Understanding can be compiled mono- and multilingually from lexical resources and datasets. The position involves designing and compiling such benchmarks in close collaboration with DSL and the other European partners of the project and to apply them in diverse evaluation scenarios. A particular focus will be put on benchmarking word understanding capabilities and on the understanding of figurative language, including the cultural bias that this part of the language may evoke in LLMs.

  Ideal candidates for this work have a background in computational lexicography and/or computational linguistics, with experience in lexicographical work and with good programming skills. It is an advantage although not a requirement, if the candidate has good knowledge of the Danish language.

  Teaching qualifications are not a requirement, since the candidate will not be involved in teaching.

  Qualification requirements
 Applicants will primarily be assessed on their research qualifications, including publications, the ability to conduct independent research and participate in research collaborations, and experience in research management. In addition, the applicant’s research plan and research potential will be assessed in relation to the project described above.

 Once the deadline for applications has expired, the Head of Section will consider advice from the appointment committee and select applicants for assessment. The Department of Psychology and Behavioural Sciences invites applications for associate professorships in Psychology. The associate professorships are full-time and permanent positions, starting in June 2027 or as soon as possible subject to mutual agreement. Applicants will be shortlisted for full assessment based on their qualifications and the Department’s need for broad recruitment across the subfields. The final number of positions to be filled will depend on the assessment of the applicants.

Job description
The announced associate professorships are permanent positions with research and teaching obligations within the specified fields outlined above. The positions come with 50 % teaching, 40 % research and 10 % administration. The successful candidate is expected to take on responsibility for research leadership in the dedicated field, publish in international peer-reviewed journals, attract external funding, develop courses and methods, participate in the Department's day-to-day activities (lecturing, seminars, workshop collaborations, etc.), undertake supervision of students and PhD students as well as participate in administrative and organizational tasks.

Your qualifications
To be considered for shortlisting, applicants must indicate which specific subfield (and potentially another supplemental subfield) they want to apply within.

Relevant candidates are expected to have published a substantial amount of research at a high international level as well as high-quality teaching within the subfield specified by the applicants.

As the successful candidates must participate in all of the department's main activities, including teaching, examination and administration related to the subfield, non-Danish speaking candidates are required to acquire the necessary language skills within a short period of time (max. 2 years).

Permanent employment as associate professor at Aarhus BSS requires completion of, within a two year period, the supervision course and also the course Online and blended learning provided by Centre for Educational Development at Aarhus University.

The required qualifications are elaborated below:

1. Substantial research production at a high international level
To qualify for the position as associate professor, a substantial research production is required. Publication records can have different profiles and should be evaluated in the context of the relevant subfield(s) and in relation to the applicant’s general academic profile. However, because publication statistics display important information regarding researchers' publication merits, applicants are encouraged to provide relevant publication statistics (e.g. number of peer reviewed publications, h-index, citations etc.).

2. Didactical/pedagogical competences and experiences at a high level, including a positive, written evaluation of these competences
Teaching and supervising students at different levels is a main activity of an associate professor. It is expected that associate professors at The Department of Psychology and Behavioural Sciences are responsible and stimulating capacities in their research fields, in their teaching activities and as a colleague at the department. The Department of Psychology and Behavioural Sciences is part of Aarhus BSS, Aarhus University – a top 100 university. Aarhus BSS has achieved the triple-crown AACSB, AMBA and EQUIS accreditations.

Department of Psychology and Behavioural Sciences, Bartholins Allé 11, DK-8000 Aarhus C.

jobs.description:
Are you excited by the intersection of people, data, and AI? Join us in shaping the future of People Analytics through modern analytics engineering, meaningful workforce insights, and data-driven decision-making.

About the role

Covering for the People Analytics and Data Strategy Engineer (“Data Analyst”), you will play a key role in taking the People & Culture data experience to the next level and support Urban Partners in reaching our ambitious goal of building the urban future, together. If you get energy from working for an internationally growing company and want to be part of making a difference, you may be our new team member!

In our People & Culture Team, we are a group of 16 colleagues covering 8 countries working together to support the business stakeholders in embodying our purpose and vision of making a difference for cities and people. You will have extensive interaction with team members and colleagues across the organization, promising exposure to a diverse range of expertise.

We can guarantee a dynamic environment with skilled colleagues, offering opportunities for learning, collaboration, and personal growth. You will be a part of a powerhouse of brilliant and caring people raising the bar for the industry. Your workplace will be at our headquarters located in Copenhagen, Nordhavn. As an international team, we regularly engage with colleagues across borders, fostering a global perspective and collaborative spirit.

In this role, you will be reporting to our Head of Reward, located in Copenhagen. The majority of this role will be carried out from our office with some flexibility.

This is a parental leave cover role on a fixed-term contract until end July 2027. Please note: we are unable to sponsor visa or work permit applications for this position. Applicants are responsible for ensuring they have the necessary right to work in Denmark prior to applying.

Key responsibilities

Over the past year, we've been experimenting with what People Analytics looks like when you treat it more like modern analytics engineering than traditional HR reporting. We have built our own analytics layer in Microsoft Fabric around an SCD2 master dataset of our employee population, with a Python semantic library on top. The setup supports workforce reporting used across senior management, the Board, financial planning, sustainability reporting and investor materials.

The role spans three closely connected areas: recurring workforce reporting, traditional People Analytics, and Reward. That means you'll work with everything from headcount and attrition analysis to the compensation review, pay transparency and ad hoc workforce questions. We've also designed the environment to work closely with modern AI assistants. LLMs are used to understand existing code, explore data, debug problems and help extend the analytical layer. We think this combination of structured data, reusable analytical logic and AI-assisted development represents an interesting direction for how People Analytics can work.

As Data Analyst, it is not simply a role where you “just” run existing reports and scripts. You'll inherit a working analytical system, learn how it fits together, keep it running reliably, and extend it when new business questions arise.

At the center of the setup is a master employee-history dataset combining the SCD2 states of our core HiBob data into one resolved timeline.

It allows us to reconstruct the workforce at historical points in time, covering approximately 20 years of employee history, with many core business rules already built into the data.

On top of this sits a Python semantic library with reusable building blocks for employee populations, joiners and leavers, turnover breakdowns, workforce bridges and much more.

Python notebooks use these components to produce recurring and ad hoc outputs including HTML reports, PowerPoint materials and Excel files.

The important part is not simply knowing how to run these tools. It is understanding the logic behind them, spotting when something does not look right, and knowing how far an answer needs to be taken before it creates business value.

These will be some of your key tasks

• Deliver key parts of the Reward cycle, including the 2027 salary review and gender pay gap and pay transparency reporting

• Support the data agenda for People & Culture, with the help of your People Lead

• Monitor data quality and investigate inconsistencies before they reach reporting.

• Run recurring workforce reporting covering headcount, FTE movement, joiners, leavers and attrition

• Support FP&A, Sustainability and Capital Formation with workforce data and analysis.

• Work on broader People Analytics questions, including workforce trends, organizational development and ad hoc analysis for senior stakeholders

• Answer new workforce questions as they arise

• Make careful extensions to the Python semantic library and reporting notebooks when needed

• Work with the BI team when source data or pipeline changes affect reporting

• Keep P&C's handling of employee data GDPR-compliant

• Build awareness and capabilities for the People & Culture team on data, analysis, and tools (e.g. Fabric, PowerBI, Excel)

Your experience & skills

• You're strong in Python and genuinely enjoy using it to solve problems

• You use LLMs such as ChatGPT, Claude or Copilot extensively to understand code, explore unfamiliar systems, debug problems and work faster

• You know that AI output still needs to be tested and verified

• You're comfortable learning things you haven't seen before

• You have a strong instinct for when data looks wrong

• You're comfortable taking ownership and working with senior stakeholders

• Ideally you have experience within remuneration or broader HR

• Ability to present data insights through clear and engaging visualizations

• Comfortable working with systems, ideally HR-related platforms

Your character

We hope you are a curious and continuous learner with a positive mindset. You take initiative, enjoy tackling challenges, and look for opportunities to improve the way things are done. Attention to detail is second nature, and you bring a pragmatic, solution-oriented approach to complex problems. You're excited by how AI is transforming analytical work, while remaining focused on delivering accurate, useful, and high-quality outcomes.

Strong communication skills, diplomacy, and empathy are essential for building positive relationships across teams and functions. With a collaborative and service-minded approach, along with professional-level English skills, you thrive in a dynamic and international environment.

What we offer

Make a difference by helping create urban spaces and places that enrich people’s lives in the most sustainable way

Lead the industry with an innovator that is pioneering new approaches while raising standards and inspiring the industry

Learn and grow as part of a powerhouse of brilliant people where teamwork, feedback and different ways of thinking are at the core

Be your whole self in a purpose-driven culture with a strong sense of belonging, based on trust, celebration and caring for each other

Join us

If this opportunity interests you, we encourage you to apply as soon as possible, as applications are reviewed and interviews conducted on an ongoing basis. Application deadline: 3 November.

We are happy to answer questions for more information, so please reach out to Joe Dias at jodi@urban.partners.

We look forward to hearing from you!

**

• Hands-on analytical depth that has stayed recent: you build and defend margin baselines yourself, and master data is familiar ground.

• A track record of building governance that held: gates or lifecycle forums with thresholds that survived contested, sponsored proposals.

• Credibility in front of a CFO and a CPO in the same meeting.

**Who You Are

**

• A self-starter: you break the ice on work nobody has owned before and bring structure where there was none.

• You develop and defend your own point of view, and you change it when the evidence says so.

• Consumer-centric: you know growth comes from products people love and a brand they think of first, and you read margin through that lens. Multipliers, not mechanical levers.

• You believe finance is a strategic copilot to the business, in the room when plans are made, not after they are priced. And you see it as the essential guardrail that keeps a company strong enough to be trusted, by the people who wear the jewellery and the investors who back it.
